quotes.text: `billing_details` must include the account holder’s name
Refunds for ACH Direct Debit payments are asynchronous and take up to 3 business days to complete. ACH Direct Debit refunds can’t be canceled.
You can’t submit evidence to contest or appeal a final ACH Direct Debit dispute.

old_evidence.text: Refunds require at least 3 business days to process.

If you use custom mandates through the [Payment Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents.md), Stripe creates a dispute inquiry for your business to provide evidence for the payment in question.

findings: New raw line 15 requires account holder name in billing_details and a complete address if the merchant of record is outside the US. Current source lines 13-19 omit this operational condition. Record the merchant-of-record qualifier; do not convert it into an unconditional address requirement.

New raw lines 61-98 separate supported business locations (including CA private preview), US customers, USD presentment, crossborder coverage, and local-currency settlement for eligible Stripe accounts. Current source line 13 is compressed but its US-bank-account/USD description is not a US-only merchant rule. Concept line 10 incorrectly says ACH Direct Debit lets US businesses pull funds; update to allow the documented non-US business locations, with dated and restricted eligibility.

New raw lines 125-138 mark partial refunds unsupported and full refunds supported; old raw lines 57-59 explicitly marked refunds and partial refunds Yes/Yes. This is a material captured-page contradiction, not proof of particular-account runtime availability. The new refund prose says asynchronous refunds take up to 3 business days, versus old raw line 385 and source line 25/concept line 58 saying at least/minimum 3. Queue source and concept correction with the source-date distinction and no unsupported promise of exact receipt time.

New raw lines 154-210 distinguish final ACH disputes, which cannot be contested, from requested proof-of-authorization inquiries with warning_needs_response, one evidence submission, and bank decision. Source line 21 places final disputes and Submit evidence in one clause; qualify that evidence route as an inquiry only. Preserve personal 60-calendar-day/business 2-business-day general windows, rare late returns, mandate invalidation, and subsequent-payment block.

New raw lines 9, 18-20, 31-40 and 330-338 distinguish instant provisional access and bank-account verification from delayed success/failure acknowledgement and funds settlement. Standard T+4 and eligible US-user T+2 have separate Eastern cutoffs; bank payout follows account payout schedule. Avoid interpreting verification or provisional access as guaranteed settlement. Source lines 13 and 17 should retain cutoff and eligibility scope.

Mandates remain required before debit. Hosted Checkout, Payment Element and invoice flows display and record the mandate; custom Payment Intents forms must show terms before confirmation. A Nacha copy of mandate is required; Stripe default email is conditional on a billing email, and custom notifications plus microdeposit reminders have separate obligations (new raw lines 211-306). Source line 19 overstates that Nacha requires an email specifically. Preserve active mandate checks for blocked accounts and Connect cloning/on_behalf_of boundaries.

New raw lines 340-362 add structured UI/product/API support, including Express Checkout Element, in-app payments, Customer Portal and Managed Payments exclusions. These are captured-page product support assertions, not account-specific entitlement. New lines 389-401 add no debit-failure fee for Stripe-initiated automatic Billing retries while preserving max two within 40 days for insufficient funds.
substantive_changes: Added merchant-of-record-dependent billing_details name/address condition (new line 15).
Expanded eligibility matrix, CA private preview, restrictions, US customer and USD presentment with distinct business settlement-country wording (new lines 60-98).
Refund capability reversed for partial refunds between old line 59 and new line 126; new asynchronous up-to-three-business-day, noncancellable refund and status handling (new lines 125-150).
Clarified final disputes versus pre-decision proof-of-authorization inquiries and evidence response route (new lines 154-210).
Structured product support, Connect and Billing retry qualifications added or reorganized (new lines 340-401).
historical_claims_to_preserve: ACH is a reusable delayed-notification, nonguaranteed US-bank-account debit; success/failure acknowledgement can take up to four business days (old lines 8-10; new line 9).
Standard settlement T+4 at 21:00 US/Eastern and faster T+2 at 14:00 only for eligible US users; payout schedule follows settlement (old lines 151-162; new lines 29-40).
Customer authorization mandate and verification precede debits; manual entry can use microdeposits with ten-day verification window (old lines 188-200; new lines 211-223 and 330-338).

Personal/business dispute windows, final ACH-network outcome, rare late returns, first dispute invalidating mandate, and later-payment dispute blocking bank-account reuse (old lines 286-302; new lines 154-176).
Connect capability and merchant-of-record boundaries, mandate cloning notice, and on_behalf_of restriction (old lines 412-453; new lines 365-387).
conflicts: Old raw line 59 lists partial refunds Yes; new raw line 126 explicitly lists partial refunds unsupported. Capture-date disagreement must remain visible rather than silently harmonized.
Old raw line 385 and source line 25/concept line 58 say at least/minimum three business days for refunds; new raw line 138 says up to three business days.
Source line 21 implies evidence can be submitted for final disputes; new raw lines 176-178 reserve evidence for Stripe-requested authorization inquiry before bank decision.

Concept line 10 says US businesses, but old raw lines 61-102 and new raw lines 60-98 list multiple non-US business locations. Source line 19's mandate-email wording is broader than the conditional default email in old raw lines 242-247 and new raw lines 267-272.
unresolved_questions: The captured documentation does not establish a particular merchant's eligibility for faster settlement, CA preview, crossborder settlement, restricted-industry approval, or live product access.
The capture conflict on partial refunds does not identify the change's effective date or behavior of existing historical transactions; preserve both dated claims.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ach-direct-debit, the old raw line 59 says refunds and partial refunds were both supported, while new raw lines 125-138 explicitly exclude partial refunds, allow full refunds, and describe asynchronous completion taking up to three business days. [[source-stripe-ach-direct-debit]] should queue this dated correction, update its outdated minimum-three-day wording, and keep the old claim as historical evidence. New line 15 also adds the billing-details rule scoped to merchant of record outside the US.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ach-direct-debit, old raw lines 288-306 already separated final ACH disputes from proof-of-authorization inquiries, and new raw lines 160-178 state that final disputes cannot be appealed while a requested late-return inquiry can receive evidence. [[source-stripe-ach-direct-debit]] should qualify its evidence sentence accordingly. New raw lines 61-98 distinguish non-US eligible business locations, CA private preview, US customers and USD presentment; old raw lines 61-102 likewise listed non-US merchants, so the linked concept's US-business wording needs correction without promising account eligibility.
